title: A run survives the host's tool-call limit — Codex's five minutes included
name: A run survives the host's tool-call
description: Reported: in Codex, work stops with a message that a five-minute limit was reached. SOBER's own limits are 30 minutes (`dispatch.timeoutMinutes` in `packages/core/src/config.ts`, `WHILE_THEY_THINK` in `packages/mcp/src/ask.ts`), so the limit is the host's: the MCP `run` tool in `packages/mcp/src/tools/build.ts` blocks until the run ends and relies on progress notifications to keep the call alive, which only works where the client sends a progressToken and resets its timer on progress. Start by reproducing it in Codex and recording which call hits the limit and the exact text. Then change `run` the way the bound decision says, so a run longer than five minutes ends as finished (or failed for its own reason) and the session learns the outcome. Tests next to the tool (`packages/mcp/src/**/*.test.ts`) must cover a run that outlasts a short simulated host limit.

brief.approach:
The decision is `block-raise`: `run` keeps blocking; the host's tool-call timeout is raised where SOBER ships the host's config. Reading done for this brief: Codex's per-server config is `McpServerConfig` (codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs) with `tool_timeout_sec: Option<Duration>` (seconds, default null → Codex's built-in limit), and a plugin's `mcpServers` — inline or via `"mcpServers": "./.mcp.json"` — takes "MCP server config objects" of that same shape (plugin-json-spec.md). So the key belongs in `packages/codex-plugin/.mcp.json`, nowhere else.

1. `packages/codex-plugin/.mcp.json`: add `"tool_timeout_sec": 1860` to the `sober` entry — `dispatch.timeoutMinutes` (30, `packages/core/src/config.ts`) plus a minute, so SOBER's own timeout fires first and the run ends as `failed` for its own reason, never as a host cut. Leave `packages/claude-code-plugin/.mcp.json` and Cursor's `mcp.json` untouched: Claude Code resets its timer on progress notifications (this session moved a 120 s `run` to the background and reported its end) and the key is not theirs.

2. `packages/codex-plugin/README.md`, under "What is different from Claude Code": one paragraph — Codex cuts a tool call at its own limit unless the server names one; the plugin sets `tool_timeout_sec` to outlast `dispatch.timeoutMinutes`; a person who raises `timeoutMinutes` past 30 raises this too, in `~/.codex/config.toml` under `[mcp_servers.sober]` if the plugin's file is not theirs to edit; the hosted ChatGPT client may cap calls whatever the config says (the decision's known cost).

3. `test/integration/plugin.test.ts`, test "every host declares the server the CLI publishes": the exact-equality assertion on the codex file becomes `toMatchObject({ mcpServers: { sober: server } })` plus an explicit `expect(codex.mcpServers.sober.tool_timeout_sec).toBeGreaterThan(DEFAULT_CONFIG.dispatch.timeoutMinutes * 60)` read from `@besober/core`, so the two numbers cannot drift apart silently. Claude and Cursor keep `toEqual`.

4. `packages/mcp/src/tools/build.ts`: no code change is needed for the decision, and the node's "reproduce in Codex" step cannot run headless — record what was verified instead: a comment beside the progress notification (line ~112) naming the Codex key and the README paragraph as where the limit is handled, so the next reader does not look for a detach path. No new test in `packages/mcp` — there is no behaviour to test; the integration test is the check.

Out of scope: any change to `run`'s contract, the skills' wording (node the-skills-and-the-codex-readme-say-what-7qz5 does that), and the hosted-client cap.

acceptance.proves: The Codex plugin names a tool-call timeout that outlasts SOBER's 30-minute dispatch timeout
The key went only where the host reads it; Claude Code and Cursor are untouched
The README says what the limit is and what to change when timeoutMinutes goes up
The plugin test asserts the timeout against DEFAULT_CONFIG.dispatch.timeoutMinutes and every other host check still holds
